Greats Sneakers - Customer Case Study Greats is a New York–based startup sneaker brand that launched a beta site in August. With no marketing budget, founders Ryan Babenzien and Jon Buscemi focused on design and experience, building an Instagram “mood board” from May 8 that grew to 8,400+ followers and established the brand’s aesthetic before products were even available. They chose Shopify to build a clean, cohesive store quickly, using their clear visual vision to guide site flow and logistics. The approach paid off: on launch day (Aug 6) they surpassed first-month sales projections within 30 hours and earned coverage in GQ, Uncrate, Hypebeast, Highsnobiety and WWD in the first three days.

Greats focused on Facebook, Instagram, and email as their primary acquisition channels during their DTC-first phase. Who are Greats' main competitors? Greats' main competitors include Atoms, Koio, and Oliver Cabell in the Italian-made premium men's sneaker segment. What makes Greats' ads effective? The price-versus-quality transparency argument — DTC prices on Italian-made sneakers — is a concrete, verifiable claim that outperforms vague luxury positioning. Who owns Greats now? Greats was acquired by Steve Madden in 2019.

About Greats Greats is a New York DTC sneaker brand, the first to go fully direct-to-consumer at a premium price with Italian-made product. Acquired by Steve Madden in 2019, Greats pioneered the DTC footwear playbook that dozens of brands subsequently copied.

Greats Ads Strategy: What Makes Greats Ads Effective Greats' paid ads led with a single price-versus-quality argument: Italian-made sneakers at DTC prices versus retail-marked-up designer alternatives. The transparency of that argument converted price-conscious quality buyers efficiently. Explore Greats ads on AdLibrary.
